title: Topic Modeling for Short Texts with Large Language Models
venue: Proceedings of ACL 2024 (Volume 4: Student Research Workshop)
read_from: ACL Anthology PDF; extended version arXiv 2406.00697 also read
task: Short-text topic modelling with prompted LLMs
problem: Short texts lack co-occurrence for conventional topic models, and LLM context limits prevent processing a whole corpus at once.
architecture: Documents are split into equal subsets below the context limit. Parallel prompting: topics per subset, then an LLM merges them. Sequential prompting: each subset is processed with the topics found so far. New metrics: document coverage (share of documents covered by the topics) and factuality (share of topic words present in the documents).
key_results: GPT-4 gives the best Cv, e.g. GoogleNewsT K = 5: 0.618 vs BERTopic 0.439.
Lower document coverage than baselines, e.g. StackOverFlow K = 15: GPT-4 0.754 vs LDA 0.842, indicating shortcuts.
Factuality stays high (e.g. GPT-4Seq 0.951 on GoogleNewsT K = 15); most non-existent topic words are synonyms or derivatives of document words.
strengths: Handles corpora larger than the context window; introduces reusable coverage and factuality metrics.

limitations.text: Only closed GPT models; training-data contamination cannot be ruled out; Llama 2 did not follow the output format; no per-document topic assignment yet.
Evaluated on 1000-document subsets per prompting run; no human evaluation.

notes: Extended version: Doi, Isonuma, Yanaka, 'Comprehensive Evaluation of Large Language Models for Topic Modeling', arXiv 2406.00697 (logged as FT2 duplicate version). The extended version adds a controllability test: category-specific prompts raise coverage of the target category (computer 0.925 vs 0.621 with the base prompt) but stay below an oracle (0.968) and lower factuality.
